# 📦 @goodandready/dsh-opencode-provider

OpenCode Console & OpenCode Go LLM Provider for DeepSeek Harness

⭐ If you like this plugin, please star it on GitHub — it shows me that the plugin is useful to you and motivates me to keep developing it.

🐛 If you find a bug or would like to request a feature, open a GitHub issue in any language — I will review your proposal and implement useful suggestions in a future plugin version.
--- OpenCode / OpenCode Go provider plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/) (dsh). It registers two native LLM routes: | Route | Product | Base | |---|---|---| | `opencode-direct` | OpenCode Console / Zen (pay-as-you-go) | `https://opencode.ai/inference` | | `opencode-go-direct` | OpenCode Go / Go Plus subscription | `https://opencode.ai/inference/go` | Requests resolve the key per call, so a changed credential reaches the next request without a restart. The ids use the `-direct` suffix because the built-in `llm-pi-ai` catalog already owns `opencode` and `opencode-go`. Reusing those ids makes the core registry reject the duplicate (`DUPLICATE_DIRECTORY`) and drop the built-in catalog, which hides the other providers and disables the add button. Existing sessions recorded under the old ids stay on the built-in routes; select **OpenCode (plugin)** or **OpenCode Go (plugin)** for this plugin's accounts, quotas, fallback and telemetry. ## Architecture ```mermaid graph LR subgraph DSH["DeepSeek Harness Core"] Agent["DSH Agent / Chat"] Creds["Credentials / auth.json"] end subgraph Plugin["dsh-opencode-provider"] Router{"Route Selector"} Pool["Multi-Account Pool
(Auto-Rotation & Cooldowns)"] Heatmap["Heatmap & Quota Telemetry
(5h / Week / Month)"] subgraph Transports["4 Wire Transports"] T1["OpenAI Chat"] T2["Anthropic Messages
(Thinking Signatures)"] T3["OpenAI Responses"] T4["Google GenAI
(thoughtSignature Replay)"] end end subgraph OpenCode["OpenCode Gateway"] Console["opencode-direct (Console / Zen)"] Go["opencode-go-direct (Go / Go Plus)"] end Agent --> Router Creds -.-> Pool Router -->|opencode-direct| Pool Router -->|opencode-go-direct| Pool Pool --> Heatmap Pool --> Transports T1 & T2 & T3 & T4 --> Console & Go ``` ## What works - **Four wire transports**, chosen per model: - OpenAI Chat Completions (DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, MiMo, LongCat, Hy3, Step, …). - Anthropic Messages (Claude Haiku, MiniMax, Qwen). - OpenAI Responses (GPT, Grok, Muse). - Google Generative AI (Gemini). - **Text, reasoning, streamed tool calls, usage, finish reasons.** - **Images** through the durable attachment service, rendered natively per transport; **file attachments** are projected to DSH's deterministic handle text (the harness supplies the read-only execution path), never inline bytes. - **Tool-result images** are inlined by Anthropic, OpenAI Responses and Google; OpenAI Chat keeps the text placeholder because its tool message has no image part. - **Replay of provider metadata** where the endpoint requires it: - Anthropic thinking signatures. - Gemini `thoughtSignature` on historical function calls. - **Multi-account rotation** before a stream starts: up to 20 accounts in drag-and-drop priority order, 401/403/429 and quota/usage-limit bodies (400/402/403/429). An invalid key cools down for 5 minutes, a quota rejection for 10 minutes or `Retry-After`, a rate limit for 60s or `Retry-After`. The account that served the last request is promoted for following conversations and survives restarts. A request already streaming is never replayed on another account; the next request uses the next usable key. - **Per-account quotas**: each account row shows its own 5-hour / weekly / monthly usage, the active account drives the sidebar and quota panel, and the panel lists every account side by side. - **Per-account runway**: estimates time to exhaustion from the average burn rate of each window and marks the first window projected to run out before its reset; approximate because the API exposes only the current percentage and reset time. - **Model → account rules**: first matching glob pins a preferred account for that model; the other accounts remain fallbacks if it fails or is cooling. - **Per-model overrides**: context window and output cap can be changed per model in Settings; `0` omits the output cap for that model. - **Request heatmap** in the quota panel: a Monday-first weekday × hour grid in local time, plus a 24-hour aggregate strip underneath. Selectors switch between all requests, any single model, and any single account. A per-account table shows requests, errors and average latency/TTFT. The adapter appends `{at, provider, model, purpose?, account, reason, ok, latencyMs, ttftMs?, error?}` to `~/.dsh/storages/dsh-opencode/requests.jsonl`; no prompt, response or key is stored. Auxiliary `session-title`/`compaction` calls are excluded from the heatmap and exact duplicate records collapse. The log compacts at 2 MB to the newest 5000 lines. Collection starts with this build — the projection cache only has `lastPromptAt`, not per-request timestamps. - **Stable `x-opencode-session`** derived from the durable session id, so retries and every turn of a conversation reuse the same routing key. - **Live catalog** from `/v1/models` with a generated `models.dev` fallback. - **Proxy support**: one live `proxyUrl` setting routes inference, model discovery and usage checks through HTTP, HTTPS or SOCKS5; the dispatcher is reused until the address changes. `proxyUsername` and a password stored in the credential service add Basic auth for both HTTP and SOCKS5. Passwords are never returned to the browser. - **Route switches**: enable or disable the Console/Zen and Go/Go Plus routes independently; a disabled route is removed from the picker and refuses requests. At least one route stays enabled. - **Per-model subscription limits** from the OpenCode Go pricing table: monthly dollar allowance plus estimated requests for the 5-hour, weekly and monthly windows, for both Go and Go Plus. Shown in the model picker and the settings page; estimates only — the gateway remains the authority. - **`/opencode` command** for status, usage, accounts, models, rules, and `test [model]`. - **TUI settings section** for the terminal profile (`/settings → OpenCode`) with the key, endpoints, proxy, allowlist, active account, fallback model, sticky routing and timeouts. - **Quota fallback**: choose a free model in Settings → OpenCode; a Go quota rejection retries once through Console/Zen. - **Sticky account**: the last successful account is preferred for the same conversation and survives restarts via a local `sticky.json` (hashed session ids and key fingerprints only); explicit model rules and pinned accounts win. - **Routing trace** in the quota panel and per-account heatmap filter. - **One-click plugin update** in Settings → OpenCode: current/latest version, an update badge, and an **Update now** button that installs the exact npm version through the DSH CLI and asks for a restart. The host endpoint is `GET/POST /dsh-opencode/update`. - **Plan-aware Go picker**: hides models outside the Go table unless turned off; descriptions carry `Go`, `Console` or `FREE`. - **Request-wide image budget** (newest images win, oldest become an omitted placeholder) and **object-root tool-schema normalization** for MCP/third-party tools. - **Usage analytics dashboard** in the quota panel: KPI cards (requests, tokens, success, input/output, reasoning, cache, TTFT, latency, errors), a 7/30/90 selector, and Models / Days / Sessions tables. Success and error cards show `—`: the local projection does not expose failed attempts or reasoning tokens. - **Usage by model** from the local session projection cache: sessions and tokens per OpenCode model. Only numeric metadata is read; titles and message content stay local. - **On-screen indicators off by default**: All UI badges, buttons and ambient alerts (`usageDisplay` in sidebar footer, `showSwitchNotice` under composer) are initially disabled. Enable them in Settings → OpenCode. - **Browser UI**: - **Settings → OpenCode**: key status, paste/import/clear, quota bars, accounts, model allowlist, per-model transport overrides, connection settings. - **Sidebar quota card** (`Off` by default; enable in Settings → OpenCode): a ring with the active account and the highest window, then 5-hour / weekly / monthly rows with remaining quota, reset countdown and bars; clicking opens the full quota panel in the center column. The panel scrolls internally, so the heatmap and usage table below the fold stay reachable. - **Cost** is shown only by DSH's native cost display; the plugin does not add a second composer pill. - Model price badges in the settings page; the OpenCode auth-entry field autocompletes from `auth.json`. - Host routes under `/dsh-opencode/*` serve state and accept writes with same-origin and JSON checks; loopback peers are trusted, and non-loopback profiles require an admin token. `GET /dsh-opencode/health` reports provider registration, accounts and model count. - The provider keeps core harness tools (`read`, `write`, `edit`, `bash`, `glob`, `grep`, …) when a large MCP set is trimmed to OpenCode's 128-tool limit. ## Install Build and pack first: ```bash npm install npm run build npm pack ``` Install the **packed tarball** into a profile: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/goodandready-dsh-opencode-provider-0.5.41.tgz # DSH Desktop: dsh plugin --profile desktop add /absolute/path/to/goodandready-dsh-opencode-provider-0.5.41.tgz # Or install the published package: dsh plugin --profile web add @goodandready/dsh-opencode-provider@0.5.41 ``` Restart dsh (or DSH Desktop), then pick **OpenCode (plugin)** or **OpenCode Go (plugin)** in the model picker. > **Use the tarball, not the directory.** On dsh 0.2.1-rc.2 the Desktop CLI aliases a local > directory passed to `dsh plugin add` as `@deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop-runtime` and overwrites > the target's `package.json`. Installing the packed `.tgz` avoids that path and installs > the package under its real name. ## Verified in DSH Desktop Tested against DSH **0.2.2-rc.1** (all 0.2.2 releases are admitted by the compatibility range) and regression-tested on **0.2.1-rc.2/rc.4**: both routes activate, model discovery returns the live catalog, and a real `deepseek-v4.1-flash` request returns `OK`. The historical Desktop verification below was captured on 0.2.1-rc.4 (and retained rc.2/rc.3 compatibility): - the plugin loads and `/dsh-opencode/state` returns `200`; - the key is picked up from `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json`; - the live catalog returned 37 models with prices and Go limits; - quota windows returned `rolling / weekly / monthly`; - `/dsh-opencode/analytics` scanned 7 local sessions (0 OpenCode sessions yet, as expected before the first OpenCode chat); - `/dsh-opencode/test` against the default flash model returned `{"ok":true,"text":"OK"}`; - a second Go account was added, the default key was temporarily replaced with an invalid one, and `/test` rotated to the second account and still returned `OK`; - the second account was already at ~98% of its monthly allowance; the rotation test pushed it over, so a later run surfaced `QUOTA`, marked the default as `invalid-credential` and `Go #2` as `quota` until its reset, with no active account; - per-account usage returned `default` 1% / 5% / 2% and `Go #2` 9% / 4% / **100%** monthly (`rate-limited`), so the exhausted account is visible without a failed request; - two `/test` requests produced `Tue 13:00 = 2` in the heatmap and two lines in `requests.jsonl`; the 24-hour strip shows the same value at 13:00; - a third request with a free-tier model added a second per-model series, so the model selector is populated; - after restarting Desktop, `Go #2` still showed its persisted `quota` cooldown while the restored default key was active; - setting `*free* → Go #2` through `/config` returned the normalized rule from `/state`, and clearing it returned `[]`; the account list stayed unchanged; - the redesigned sidebar card was checked in Desktop: `OpenCode Go` with a 5% ring, `5-Hour Window 99% remaining · 3h`, `Weekly Window 95% remaining · 6d`, `Monthly Window 98% remaining · 29d`; it uses the DSH theme variables and matches the meter's row/ring layout; - a real chat produced two OpenCode sessions: one standard flash model (4105 in / 243 out, ≈$0.00079) and one free model (10670 in / 171 out, Free); the heatmap counted 6 main requests (the two title calls and exact duplicates are filtered); - the renderer loaded the client bundle (`settings.opencode` is present in its code cache). Open **Settings → OpenCode → Sidebar** and choose **Quota display: Auto / Always / Off**. `Auto` shows the meter when OpenCode Go usage exists; `Off` stops its background polling. ## Configure ```yaml - id: llm-opencode name: "@goodandready/dsh-opencode-provider" config: apiKeyEnv: OPENCODE_API_KEY # default # apiKey: oc_sk_... # composition only, never commit openCodeAuthEntry: opencode-go requestTimeoutMs: 300000 streamIdleTimeoutMs: 300000 visibleModels: [] modelTransports: {} # contextWindowOverrides: { model-id: 65536 } # maxOutputTokens: 32768 accounts: - label: Go #2 apiKeyEnv: OPENCODE_API_KEY_2 activeAccount: '' # label or credential name to pin ``` Every field except `apiKey` is volatile and appears in dsh settings. ### Keys 1. `config.apiKey` (composition only, `role('secret')`). 2. The dsh credential seam under `apiKeyEnv`. 3. `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` → entry `openCodeAuthEntry` (default `opencode-go`), written by OpenCode's own `/connect`. 4. The launch environment (process, project `.env`, `$DSH_HOME/.env`). Extra `accounts` resolve the same way (literal key or credential reference). If you already use OpenCode, the plugin picks up the stored Go key automatically. ### Accounts and rotation Add a second account in **Settings → OpenCode → Accounts**: give it a name and a credential reference (for example `OPENCODE_API_KEY_2`), paste its key, then Save. The default account (the key card at the top) always serves first unless `activeAccount` pins another one. Rotation happens **before any content is streamed**. When the serving key is rejected with an invalid credential, a rate limit, or an exhausted quota, the adapter marks that key and retries the same request with the next usable account. An exhausted pinned account still falls back to the others; it returns to service once its cooldown passes. A request that has already started streaming is not replayed on another account. Each account row shows the current cooldown (`Invalid key`, `Quota cooldown · 23h`, `Rate limited · 30s`) and its own quota chips. The active marker moves to the first account that is not cooling down. The last account is marked too, so a failed turn explains which key ended it. Quota cooldowns honor the provider's reset (`Retry-After`) when present. The quota panel repeats the numbers in an accounts table, and the sidebar meter uses the active account. Cooldowns survive restarts: deadlines and reasons are stored in `~/.dsh/storages/dsh-opencode/cooldowns.json` keyed by a SHA-256 fingerprint — raw keys are never written. Expired entries are dropped on load, and the file keeps at most 50 entries. ### Model → account rules Pin a model to a preferred account with a glob. The first matching rule wins; `*` and `?` are supported and matching is case-insensitive. The named account is tried first, and the other accounts remain fallbacks if it is cooling, missing, or rejected — a rule is a preference, not a hard filter. An unknown account label is ignored, and rules apply to both `opencode-direct` and `opencode-go-direct`. Configure them in **Settings → OpenCode → Model → account rules**, or in YAML: ```yaml modelAccountRules: - pattern: "*free*" account: "free" - pattern: "your-provider-*" account: "go" ``` The account label is the same one shown in **Accounts** (`default` or the extra account's name). ### Request heatmap The quota panel has a **Request heatmap**: rows are Monday–Sunday, columns are local-time hours, and each cell counts calls made through this adapter (including tool-loop steps and `Test connection`). Auxiliary `session-title` and `compaction` calls are excluded, and exact duplicate records collapse; tool-loop steps are separate adapter requests, so one chat message is not necessarily one cell. Hover a cell to see the exact count. A 24-hour strip below the grid aggregates the same window by hour across all days, so the daily shape stays readable even when the grid is sparse. When more than one model or account has traffic, selectors switch the grid and strip to a single model or account; each option shows its total. The data is append-only metadata in `~/.dsh/storages/dsh-opencode/requests.jsonl`; it never includes prompts, responses or keys. Because the local projection cache stores only the last prompt time per session, the heatmap starts collecting with this build and grows as you use the plugin. ## Settings page Open **Settings → OpenCode**: - **Key** — status, paste a new key, import the key OpenCode already stored, clear it, or run a **Test connection** against a chosen model and see the latency and reply. - **Quota** — 5-hour, weekly and monthly bars with reset dates, plus warning banners at 80% and 95%. - **Accounts** — add extra accounts by credential reference, set each account's key from the page, see whether it is configured, pin one, or return to automatic rotation. **Import all from auth.json** copies every OpenCode key into its own credential ref and adds an account for it; **Check all accounts** refreshes the per-account quota/health rows. - **Models** — search, refresh the live catalog, uncheck models to build an allowlist, override the wire transport per model, and see each model's input/output price plus its Go request estimate (`Go 34.7K/5h`). Hover the estimate for the full Go / Go Plus monthly allowance and 5h/week/month request counts; expand **Subscription limits** for a table of every model with both plans. - **Connection** — API bases, usage endpoint, timeouts, output cap, context override. The OpenCode auth-entry field autocompletes from the keys present in `auth.json`. - **Sidebar** — quota display mode `Auto` / `Always` / `Off`. The card refreshes after saving and every 60 seconds while enabled. - **Plugin update** — current/latest version, update badge, and **Update now**. It installs the exact registry version through the normal `dsh plugin add` path, blocks a second click while installing, and reports when DSH must be restarted. - **Routing** — sticky account per conversation and the free fallback model used after a Go quota error. The quota panel shows the last routing decisions with their reason. The sidebar quota card defaults to **Auto**: it appears when Go usage exists and can be set to **Always** or **Off** under **Sidebar**. Clicking it opens the full quota panel with the **Usage by model** table (7/30/90-day window). The Host serves `/dsh-opencode/state`, `/health`, `/analytics`, `/config`, `/key`, `/key/clear`, `/auth-import`, `/refresh`, `/models/refresh`, `/test` and `/update`. Writes require JSON and same-origin Host/Origin. Loopback peers are trusted; a LAN/web profile must set `adminToken` or `OPENCODE_ADMIN_TOKEN`, after which every `/dsh-opencode/*` route requires `x-opencode-token` or `Authorization: Bearer`. The UI prompts for the token once and keeps it in this browser. ## Updates The **Plugin update** card in Settings → OpenCode calls `GET /dsh-opencode/update`, which compares the installed `package.json` with the npm registry. When a newer version exists, **Update now** sends the same-origin request with `x-dsh-plugin-update: 1`; the Host runs the normal DSH CLI: ```text dsh plugin --profile add --config.minimumReleaseAge=0 @goodandready/dsh-opencode-provider@ ``` The update is blocked while another update is running, never uses `--force`, and never installs from a worktree or a `file:` path. The card reports that DSH must be restarted after a successful install. If the runtime does not expose the CLI entry, the card says that automatic update is unavailable and points to the DSH plugin manager; the status check still works. ## Visual verification ![OpenCode quota and analytics panel](media/visual-verification.png) Captured from the exact 0.5.0 release candidate in DSH Desktop in the dark theme. ## Command ``` /opencode status # accounts, per-account quotas, rules /opencode usage # quota windows only /opencode accounts # labels, source, active/cooling, 5h/wk/mo /opencode models # ids, FREE/Go limits /opencode rules # model → account rules /opencode test [model] # minimal real request ``` Set **Settings → OpenCode → `/opencode` command language** to `中文` to localize this output. The default is English. ## Verified API facts - `GET /inference/go/v1/models` is public and returns the live Go roster. - `GET /zen/go/v1/usage` returns `rolling` (5h), `weekly`, `monthly` with `percent` and `resetsAt`. It is undocumented; the plugin treats it as fail-open. - The unified `POST /zen/go/v1/chat/completions` accepts OpenAI-compatible **and** Anthropic-backed models, but **not** Responses-only or Google models. - Responses-only models and Gemini need their native endpoints, which the plugin uses. - Gemini requires replaying `thoughtSignature` on historical function calls; the Google transport stores it in dsh's replay state. - `x-opencode-session` is mandatory. Недействительный ключ охлаждается 5 минут, превышение квоты — 10 минут (или по заголовку `Retry-After`), rate limit — 60 секунд (или по `Retry-After`). Аккаунт, обслуживший последний запрос, поднимается первым для следующих диалогов и сохраняется после рестарта. - Если запрос уже начал стриминг, он не переключается посреди ответа; следующий запрос берёт следующий готовый ключ. - **Sidebar-карточка квот**: режим **Auto / Always / Off** в разделе **Sidebar**; `Auto` показывает карточку при наличии Go-расхода, `Off` останавливает фоновый polling. - **Квоты по каждому аккаунту**: отображение индивидуального расхода за 5 часов, неделю и месяц; активный аккаунт управляет сайдбаром и панелью. - **Runway по каждому аккаунту**: оценка времени до исчерпания по среднему темпу каждого окна; отмечается первое окно, которое закончится раньше сброса. Оценка приблизительная: API отдаёт только текущий процент и время сброса. - **Онбординг аккаунтов**: **Import all from auth.json** переносит все ключи OpenCode в отдельные credential ref и добавляет аккаунты; **Check all accounts** обновляет квоты и health по каждому аккаунту. - **Правила «модель ➔ аккаунт»**: сопоставление по glob-паттернам закрепляет предпочтительный аккаунт за моделью; остальные аккаунты остаются в резерве. - **Per-model overrides**: контекст и лимит вывода настраиваются для каждой модели; `0` убирает лимит вывода. - **Квотный fallback**: выберите бесплатную модель в настройках; при ошибке квоты Go тот же запрос один раз повторяется через Console/Zen. Если fallback тоже не сработал, возвращается исходная ошибка квоты. - **Липкий аккаунт**: последний успешный аккаунт предпочитается в том же диалоге и сохраняется между перезапусками в локальном `sticky.json` (только хешированные session id и fingerprint ключей); явные правила модели, закреплённый аккаунт и квотный fallback имеют приоритет. - **Трассировка маршрутизации**: панель квот показывает последние решения (`rule`, `sticky`, `rotation`, `quota-fallback`) без промптов и ключей. - **Статистика по аккаунтам**: в request log пишутся `ok`, `latencyMs`, `ttftMs` и `error`; heatmap показывает таблицу запросов, ошибок и средних latency/TTFT по каждому аккаунту. - **Почасовой Heatmap запросов**: сетка «день недели × час» в локальном времени плюс суточная полоса агрегации. Фильтры переключают отображение между всеми запросами, конкретной моделью и аккаунтом. Лог `~/.dsh/storages/dsh-opencode/requests.jsonl` хранит только метаданные `{at, provider, model, purpose, account, reason, ok, latencyMs, ttftMs, error}` (промпты и ответы не сохраняются). - **Стабильный заголовок `x-opencode-session`**: вычисляется из устойчивого ID сессии DSH, обеспечивая одинаковый ключ маршрутизации при повторах и диалоге. - **Живой каталог моделей**: автоматическое чтение `/v1/models` с резервным fallback из `models.dev`. - **Proxy**: live-параметр `proxyUrl` направляет инференс, каталог и проверку квот через HTTP, HTTPS или SOCKS5; dispatcher переиспользуется до смены адреса. `proxyUsername` и пароль из credential-сервиса включают Basic auth для HTTP и SOCKS5. Пароль не возвращается в браузер. - **Переключатели маршрутов**: Console/Zen и Go/Go Plus включаются и отключаются независимо; отключённый маршрут исчезает из выбора и отклоняет запросы. Хотя бы один маршрут остаётся включённым. - **Оценки лимитов подписки OpenCode Go**: долларовый лимит и расчетное число запросов для окон 5h, недели и месяца для планов Go и Go Plus. - **Команда `/opencode`**: быстрый просмотр статуса, квот, аккаунтов, моделей, правил и запуск теста связи `test [model]`. - **Настройки в терминале (TUI)**: раздел `/settings → OpenCode` для профиля terminal с ключом, эндпоинтами, allowlist, активным аккаунтом, fallback-моделью, sticky-маршрутизацией и таймаутами. - **Интеграция с Settings → Models**: стандартные карточки OpenCode/OpenCode Go; ключ задаётся только через «Изменить». - **One-Click обновление плагина**: кнопка **Update now** в настройках проверяет npm registry, ставит точную версию через DSH CLI и запрашивает перезапуск. - **Plan-aware Go picker**: фильтрация моделей вне тарифной сетки Go с бейджами `Go`, `Console` или `FREE`. - **Защита лимита MCP-инструментов**: сохраняет системные инструменты DSH (`read`, `write`, `edit`, `bash`, `glob`, `grep`) при сокращении сторонних инструментов под лимит 128. - **Панель аналитики использования**: карточки KPI (запросы, токены, успешность, reasoning, кэш, TTFT, задержка), фильтр 7/30/90 дней и таблицы Models / Days / Sessions. ## Установка Сборка и упаковка из исходников: ```bash npm install npm run build npm pack ``` Установка из **упакованного tarball**: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/goodandready-dsh-opencode-provider-0.5.41.tgz # DSH Desktop: dsh plugin --profile desktop add /absolute/path/to/goodandready-dsh-opencode-provider-0.5.41.tgz # Либо установка опубликованного пакета из npm: dsh plugin --profile web add @goodandready/dsh-opencode-provider@0.5.41 ``` После установки перезапустите dsh (или DSH Desktop) и выберите **OpenCode (plugin)** или **OpenCode Go (plugin)** в списке моделей. ## Конфигурация Пример файла конфигурации: ```yaml - id: llm-opencode name: "@goodandready/dsh-opencode-provider" config: apiKeyEnv: OPENCODE_API_KEY # переменная окружения или имя credential # apiKey: oc_sk_... # только для локальной сборки, не коммитить! openCodeAuthEntry: opencode-go requestTimeoutMs: 300000 streamIdleTimeoutMs: 300000 visibleModels: [] modelTransports: {} accounts: - label: Go #2 apiKeyEnv: OPENCODE_API_KEY_2 activeAccount: '' # метка аккаунта для принудительного закрепления ``` ### Источники ключей 1. `config.apiKey` в конфигурации DSH (`role('secret')`). 2. Системные учетные данные DSH по имени `apiKeyEnv`. 3. Авто-импорт из `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` (по ключу `openCodeAuthEntry`, по умолчанию `opencode-go`), записанный CLI-утилитой OpenCode. 4. Переменные окружения процесса, проекта `.env` или `$DSH_HOME/.env`. ### Настройка пула аккаунтов и ротации Добавьте второй аккаунт в **Настройки → OpenCode → Accounts**: укажите метку (например, `Go #2`) и имя переменной/credential (`OPENCODE_API_KEY_2`), вставьте ключ и сохраните. Аккаунт по умолчанию (`default`) всегда обслуживает запросы первым, если не закреплен другой. При ошибке авторизации, исчерпании лимита или rate limit адаптер помечает ключ периодом охлаждения (cooldown) и немедленно повторяет запрос со следующим доступным аккаунтом. Состояния cooldown сохраняются между перезапусками в `~/.dsh/storages/dsh-opencode/cooldowns.json` по SHA-256 хешу ключа — сырые токены на диск не записываются. ### Правила привязки «модель ➔ аккаунт» С помощью glob-паттернов можно закрепить определенные модели за выделенными аккаунтами: ```yaml modelAccountRules: - pattern: "*free*" account: "free" - pattern: "your-provider-*" account: "go" ``` ## Страница настроек Web UI В разделе **Настройки → OpenCode**: - **Key**: статус ключа, вставка, импорт из OpenCode CLI, очистка и кнопка **Test connection** с замером задержки. - **Quota**: шкалы расхода за 5 часов, неделю и месяц с датами сброса и предупреждениями при 80% и 95%. - **Accounts**: управление пулом дополнительных учетных записей. - **Models**: поиск, обновление каталога, фильтрация allowlist, переопределение транспорта и просмотр стоимости токенов. - **Connection**: таймауты, базовые URL, прокси, admin token и переключатели маршрутов. - **Plugin update**: статус версии и кнопка **Update now**. ## Команды CLI ```bash /opencode status # статус аккаунтов, квоты и правила /opencode usage # текущие окна квот /opencode accounts # список меток, статус и расход 5h/wk/mo /opencode models # список моделей и лимиты Go /opencode rules # правила модель ➔ аккаунт /opencode test [model] # проверочный запрос к модели ``` Язык вывода задаётся в **Настройки → OpenCode → `/opencode` command language** (`中文` включает китайский). По умолчанию английский. ### Матрица движков `npm run test:engine -- ` проверяет неизменяемый уже собранный пакет по `engines.dsh` и `dsh.compatibility.dshReleases`, а также состав production-файлов. Команда только читает: не ставит DSH, не запускает runtime, не распаковывает архив, не трогает другие плагины и не требует cleanup. Прогон совместимости выполняется на согласованном тестовом контуре MiniPC с опубликованным кандидатом — не из worktree и без принудительных процессов или рекурсивного удаления. ## Дополнительно в 0.5.22–0.5.36 - **Аутентифицированный прокси**: `proxyUsername` + пароль из credential-сервиса для HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS5; пароль не возвращается в браузер. - **Переключатели маршрутов** Console/Zen и Go/Go Plus; отключённый маршрут исчезает из picker и отклоняет запросы. - **Переопределения по моделям**: контекст, лимит вывода, транспорт; `0` убирает лимит вывода. - **Аналитика и heatmap**: запросы, токены, TTFT, задержки, модели/дни/сессии и сетка день×час; только локальные числовые метаданные. - **Режимы квоты** Auto/Always/Off, sticky-маршрутизация, `autoSwitch`, уведомление о смене аккаунта и карточка обновления. - **Admin token** для LAN/web-профиля; запросы через прокси без токена отклоняются (401 fail-closed). ## Безопасность и надежность - Same-origin — это защита от CSRF, а не аутентификация. Задайте admin-токен владельца в конфиге профиля (`adminToken`) или `OPENCODE_ADMIN_TOKEN`; тогда все маршруты `/dsh-opencode/*` требуют `x-opencode-token` или `Authorization: Bearer`.
